title: Emergency & Work Life
summary: What to say when something goes wrong: call emergency services, explain a work or shift problem, and ask for help with neighborhood issues.

units.title: Call 119 or 112 in an Emergency
units.situation: You need urgent help after an accident, sudden illness, fire, or unsafe situation.
units.goal: I can call 119 or 112, state the emergency, give my location, and ask for an interpreter if needed.

keyPhrases.note: Use for ambulance, fire, and rescue help.

keyPhrases.en: Please report it to 112 / call the police.
keyPhrases.note: Use for police help or immediate danger.

keyPhrases.en: I'm not sure where this is.
keyPhrases.note: Useful when you are lost or shaken.
Say this early if the call is difficult.
다치다 = to get injured; past form 다쳤어요.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Someone is hurt. I need interpretation.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: I'll send the address. Please come quickly.

beginnerGuide.title: 119 vs 112
beginnerGuide.body: Use 119 for ambulance, fire, rescue, and medical emergencies. Use 112 for police help, violence, theft, stalking, or immediate danger. If you freeze, say 도와 주세요 first, then your location.

beginnerGuide.title: Location first
beginnerGuide.body: Korean emergency calls need your location quickly. Say the building name, subway exit, nearby store, or send the address by text if possible: 주소를 보내드릴게요.

beginnerGuide.title: Interpreter request
beginnerGuide.body: 통역이 필요해요 means “I need interpretation.” Use it early. Keep sentences short: 다쳤어요, 아파요, 불이 났어요, 위험해요.

checkpoints: I can ask for help with 도와 주세요.
I know 119 is for ambulance/fire/rescue and 112 is for police.
I can say 통역이 필요해요 and give or send my location.
I can explain injury with 사람이 다쳤어요.
steps: Move to a safer place if you can.
Call 119 for medical/fire/rescue or 112 for police.
Say the problem first: 사람이 다쳤어요 / 불이 났어요 / 위험해요.
Give your location or say 주소를 보내드릴게요.
Ask for interpretation with 통역이 필요해요.

deepLinks.label: Emergency Ready App
deepLinks.note: Multilingual emergency alerts, safety guidance, and shelter information.

units.costs: Emergency calls to 119 and 112 are free. Medical treatment or ambulance-related costs can depend on the situation and insurance.
units.notes: Save your home address in Korean in your phone. In a real emergency, showing or sending the written address can be faster than trying to pronounce it.

units.title: Call in Sick or Explain a Work Problem
units.situation: You have a part-time job, shift, class assistant job, or office role and need to explain illness, lateness, pay, or schedule trouble politely.
units.goal: I can tell a manager I am sick or late, ask about pay or schedule, and know where official labor help starts.

keyPhrases.ko: 오늘 몸이 안 좋아서 출근이 어려울 것 같아요.
keyPhrases.romanization: oneul momi an joaseo chulgeuni eoryeoul geot gatayo.
keyPhrases.en: I do not feel well today, so I think it will be hard to come to work.

keyPhrases.romanization: isip bun jeongdo neujeul geot gatayo.
keyPhrases.en: I think I will be about 20 minutes late.
I want to check my working hours.
keyPhrases.note: 근무 시간 = work hours / shift hours.

keyPhrases.en: May I check the contract again?
keyPhrases.note: A polite way to ask without sounding accusatory.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.ko: 오늘 몇 시에 올 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul myeot sie ol su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: What time can you come today?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.ko: 죄송해요. 몸이 안 좋아서 오늘 출근이 어려울 것 같아요.
dialogue.romanization: joesonghaeyo. momi an joaseo oneul chulgeuni eoryeoul geot gatayo.
dialogue.en: I am sorry. I do not feel well, so I think it will be hard to come in today.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.en: Okay. Are you okay for tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.ko: 네, 내일은 출근할 수 있을 것 같아요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, naeireun chulgeunhal su isseul geot gatayo.
dialogue.en: Yes, I think I can come to work tomorrow.

beginnerGuide.title: Use soft prediction at work
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ 것 같아요 softens a difficult message: 어려울 것 같아요, 늦을 것 같아요, 갈 수 있을 것 같아요. It sounds less blunt than 못 가요 or 늦어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Ask about money and contracts calmly
beginnerGuide.body: For pay, schedule, or contracts, use 확인하고 싶어요 or 다시 확인해도 될까요? These are neutral workplace phrases before a disagreement becomes a complaint.

beginnerGuide.title: Know the official help line
beginnerGuide.body: For labor law questions, the Ministry of Employment and Labor lists labor counseling at 1350 for domestic calls and an overseas number on its English site.

checkpoints: I can say I am sick and cannot come in today politely.
I can give a lateness estimate with 20분 정도 늦을 것 같아요.
I can ask about work hours, payday, and a contract without sounding aggressive.
I know MOEL 1350 is the official starting point for labor-law counseling.
steps: Message or call as early as possible if you are sick or late.
State the reason briefly: 몸이 안 좋아서 / 지하철이 지연돼서.
Give the expected action: 출근이 어려울 것 같아요 / 20분 늦을 것 같아요.
For money or schedule issues, ask to check details first: 확인하고 싶어요.
If it becomes a legal issue, contact MOEL labor counseling.

deepLinks.label: Ministry of Employment and Labor
deepLinks.note: Official labor information and labor-law counseling contact numbers, including 1350.

units.costs: Asking your workplace is free. Official counseling numbers may follow normal phone-rate rules depending on your plan.
units.notes: Keep screenshots of schedules, contract terms, pay dates, and messages. Clear records help if a misunderstanding becomes a formal labor question.

units.title: Noise, Lost Items, and Local Complaints
units.situation: You need help from a neighbor, building guard, local office, or city call center about noise, lost items, or a local living problem.
units.goal: I can ask politely about noise, report a lost item, and contact 120 for local help when I do not know which office handles the issue.

keyPhrases.ko: 혹시 조금만 조용히 해 주실 수 있을까요?
keyPhrases.romanization: hoksi jogeumman joyonghi hae jusil su isseulkkayo?
keyPhrases.en: Could you possibly be a little quieter?

keyPhrases.note: Swap 지갑 for 휴대폰, 카드, 여권.
Useful in subway stations, buses, airports, and malls.

keyPhrases.en: Where should I ask about this issue?
keyPhrases.note: When you do not know the right office.
120 is a city service/civil complaint help line in Seoul.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Hello. The noise is a little loud at night.

dialogue.speaker: Neighbor
dialogue.en: Oh, I am sorry. I did not know.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.ko: 괜찮아요. 혹시 조금만 조용히 해 주실 수 있을까요?
dialogue.romanization: gwaenchanayo. hoksi jogeumman joyonghi hae jusil su isseulkkayo?
dialogue.en: It is okay. Could you possibly be a little quieter?

beginnerGuide.title: Lead with 혹시 and 조금만
beginnerGuide.body: Noise and neighbor issues can sound confrontational. 혹시 and 조금만 soften the request: 혹시 조금만 조용히 해 주실 수 있을까요?

beginnerGuide.title: Lost item frame
beginnerGuide.body: Use N을/를 잃어버렸어요 for lost things: 지갑을 잃어버렸어요, 카드를 잃어버렸어요, 여권을 잃어버렸어요. Then ask 분실물 센터가 어디예요?

beginnerGuide.title: 120 as a routing helper
beginnerGuide.body: If you are in Seoul and do not know whether to ask a district office, transport office, or another city service, 120 Dasan can route general living and civil-service questions.

checkpoints: I can soften a neighbor request with 혹시 and 조금만.
I can say I lost a wallet/card/passport using 잃어버렸어요.
I can ask where the lost-and-found center is.
I know 120 can help route Seoul city-service questions and complaints.
steps: For a neighbor issue, start polite and specific: 밤에 소리가 조금 커서요.
Make a soft request: 조금만 조용히 해 주실 수 있을까요?
For a lost item, name the item and where you lost it if possible.
Ask 분실물 센터가 어디예요? at stations, malls, buses, or offices.
If you do not know the right local office, ask 120 or your building manager.

deepLinks.label: 120 Dasan Call Center
deepLinks.note: Foreign-language help for Seoul living information and civil complaints.

deepLinks.label: Seoul foreign language consultation notice
deepLinks.note: Seoul announcement about foreign-language consultation support.

units.costs: Calling 120 may follow normal phone charges depending on your plan. Lost-item storage or document replacement fees vary by place and item.
units.notes: For immediate danger, do not use 120 first — call 112 or 119. Use 120 for city-service questions, living information, or non-emergency complaints.
